title: Math
summary: The mathematics of change and of strategy.

children.title: Calculus
children.summary: The mathematics of continuous change, from limits and derivatives to integrals.

children.title: Limits
children.summary: The foundational idea of approaching a value, underpinning both derivatives and integrals.

children.title: Derivatives
children.summary: Instantaneous rates of change and the slope of a curve at a point.

children.title: Integrals
children.summary: Accumulation and area under a curve — the inverse of differentiation.

children.title: Game Theory
children.summary: The study of strategic decision-making among rational agents.

children.title: Nash Equilibrium
children.summary: A strategy profile where no player can gain by unilaterally changing their own strategy.

children.title: Dominant Strategies
children.summary: Strategies that yield a better outcome for a player regardless of what the others do.

children.title: Prisoner's Dilemma
children.summary: The classic game showing why two rational agents may fail to cooperate even when it serves them both.

children.title: The Z-Transform
children.summary: The z-transform as a landscape over the complex plane, with a 3D viewer: poles, zeros, the region of convergence and the frequency response.

children.title: Points of the z-Plane
children.summary: What z to the power −n does to a sample: a spiral that scales and turns.

children.title: The Surface |X(z)|
children.summary: Poles and zeros, and how they shape the whole landscape.

children.title: The Region of Convergence
children.summary: Rings where the sum converges, and two signals that share one formula.

children.title: The Unit Circle and Frequency Response
children.summary: The surface sliced along |z| = 1, read with a ruler.

children.title: Pole Positions and the Time Signal
children.summary: Pole radius sets the decay, pole angle the oscillation.

children.title: Properties as Geometry
children.summary: Delay, scaling, modulation, reversal and convolution as moves of the plane.

children.title: Inverting the Transform
children.summary: Partial fractions and the contour integral round a circle in the ROC.

children.title: A Gallery of Signals
children.summary: Every signal in the viewer, from its samples to its stability.

children.title: The Laplace Transform
children.summary: The Laplace transform as a landscape over the s-plane, with a 3D viewer: poles, zeros, the region of convergence, the frequency response and solving differential equations.

children.title: Points of the s-Plane
children.summary: What e to the power −st does to a signal: a turning arrow that grows or shrinks.

children.title: The Surface |X(s)|
children.summary: Poles and zeros, and how they shape the whole landscape.

children.title: The Region of Convergence
children.summary: Vertical strips where the integral converges, and two signals that share one formula.

children.title: The Imaginary Axis and Frequency Response
children.summary: The surface sliced along s = jω, read with a ruler.

children.title: Pole Positions and the Time Signal
children.summary: How far left a pole sits sets the decay, its height the oscillation.

children.title: Properties of the Transform
children.summary: Delays, shifts, scaling, derivatives, integrals, convolution and the value theorems.

children.title: Solving Differential Equations
children.summary: Derivatives become multiplication by s: circuits and springs as algebra.

children.title: Inverting the Transform
children.summary: Partial fractions, and the Bromwich integral up a line in the ROC.

children.title: A Gallery of Signals
children.summary: Every signal in the viewer, and the bridge from the s-plane to the z-plane.

children.title: The Fourier Transform
children.summary: Signals built from sinusoids, with a 3D viewer of harmonics and spectra: Fourier series, the Fourier transform, sampling and the DFT, and the fast Fourier transform.

children.title: Sinusoids and Complex Exponentials
children.summary: Amplitude, frequency and phase, and the turning arrow e to the jωt.

children.title: Fourier Series: Building a Wave
children.summary: The coefficient integral, orthogonality, and three classic waves worked out.

children.title: Reading a Spectrum
children.summary: Amplitude and phase spectra, one-sided and two-sided, and Parseval's theorem.

children.title: Convergence and the Gibbs Phenomenon
children.summary: How fast coefficients fall, and the overshoot at a jump.

children.title: From Series to Transform
children.summary: Letting the period grow: the Fourier transform, a table of pairs, and the Laplace link.

children.title: Properties of the Transform
children.summary: Shifts, scaling, modulation, convolution and the uncertainty principle.

children.title: Sampling and the DFT
children.summary: Aliasing, the Nyquist rate, the discrete Fourier transform, leakage and windows.

children.title: The Fast Fourier Transform
children.summary: Splitting a DFT into halves: from N² work to N log N, step by step.

children.title: A Gallery of Waves
children.summary: Every signal in the viewer, from waveform to spectrum.
